items.title: Global Summits 2025-26 — G20, BRICS, SCO, QUAD
items.body:
**In one line.** The hosts, themes and newest members of the four big groupings — G20, BRICS, SCO and QUAD — in 2025-26.

**Why it is asked.** Host cities, chairs and new entrants are the most-tested summit facts, and the exam swaps one grouping's host or member for another's.

**G20** (Group of Twenty — the world's 20 largest economies).
- **2025 — Johannesburg (20th):** the first G20 summit ever held in **Africa**.
- **2026 — Miami, USA (21st):** planned for **14-15 December 2026** at Trump National Doral, chaired by **Donald Trump**; the US announced (November 2025) that **South Africa would not be invited**.
- The **African Union** became a permanent G20 member during India's 2023 presidency.

**BRICS** (Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa, plus newer members).
- **India holds the 2026 chairship**, theme **'Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability'**.
- Expansion: **Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran and the UAE (2024)** and **Indonesia (2025)** joined; the acronym was coined by economist Jim O'Neill (2001); the first summit was in Russia (2009).

**SCO** (Shanghai Cooperation Organisation — a Eurasian political-security bloc).
- **2026 is under China's presidency**; the SCO was set up in 2001. Its permanent bodies are the **Secretariat (Beijing)** and **RATS**, the Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure (**Tashkent**). India and Pakistan joined in 2017, Iran in 2023.

**QUAD** (the Quadrilateral grouping of India, USA, Japan and Australia).
- The **2026 Foreign Ministers' Meeting in New Delhi** launched a **Critical Minerals Framework** (to reduce dependence on China for key minerals), plus maritime-surveillance and Pacific-port initiatives. The QUAD was formalised in 2007.

**Don't confuse.** The SCO Secretariat is in **Beijing** and RATS is in **Tashkent** — options often swap the two cities.
keyPoints: 2025 G20 (Johannesburg) was the first held in Africa; 2026 G20 is in Miami, USA (14-15 Dec 2026), chaired by Trump, with South Africa not invited.
India chairs BRICS in 2026, theme 'Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability'; Indonesia joined BRICS in 2025.
SCO 2026 is under China's presidency; its Secretariat is in Beijing and RATS in Tashkent.
The 2026 QUAD Foreign Ministers' Meet in New Delhi launched a Critical Minerals Framework to cut dependence on China.
The African Union became a permanent G20 member during India's 2023 presidency.
items.source: factbase ca-2026-08 (F-CA2608-074), ca-2025-10-and-11 (BRICS), ca-2026-05-and-04 (QUAD/SCO); Wikipedia 2026 G20 Miami summit

items.title: Climate Diplomacy — COP30 Belém & COP31 Antalya
items.body:
**In one line.** The last two UN climate summits — COP30 at Belém and COP31 at Antalya — and the rules behind them.

**Why it is asked.** COP host cities and years are repeat questions, and the unusual COP31 'Turkey hosts, Australia presides' split is a favourite trap.

**COP** stands for Conference of the Parties — the yearly meeting of countries under the UN climate treaty.

**COP30 — Belém, Brazil (2025).** Held in the Amazon city of **Belém**; India committed to a **more ambitious Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC)** — an NDC is each country's own pledge to cut emissions.

**COP31 — Antalya, Turkey (2026).**
- The **31st** UN Climate Change Conference, **9-20 November 2026**, at the Antalya Expo Center.
- The host dispute was settled by compromise: **Turkey hosts** the venue, while **Australia** (minister Chris Bowen) **presides over the negotiations**.
- A pre-COP and leaders' event were planned in **Fiji/Tuvalu (5-8 October)** to spotlight Pacific climate impacts; a World Leaders' Summit was set for Antalya on 11-12 November.
- Next: **COP32 — Addis Ababa, Ethiopia (2027)**.

**Frame for MCQs.**
- The COP is the supreme decision-making body of the **UNFCCC** — the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (1992). The **Paris Agreement (2015)** aims to keep warming well below 2°C, ideally 1.5°C.
- The **WMO** (World Meteorological Organization) reported a **91% chance** that global temperature will top 1.5°C for at least one year between 2026 and 2030.

**Don't confuse.** For COP31, Turkey is the *host venue* but Australia *presides over negotiations* — both facts can be tested in one question.
keyPoints: COP30 (2025) was held at Belém, Brazil; India pledged a more ambitious NDC there.
COP31 (9-20 Nov 2026) is hosted by Turkey at Antalya, with Australia presiding over the negotiations.
COP32 (2027) will be held at Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
The COP is the supreme decision-making body of the UNFCCC (1992); the Paris Agreement dates to 2015.
WMO: 91% chance of a year exceeding 1.5°C warming between 2026 and 2030.
items.source: Wikipedia — 2026 UN Climate Change Conference; factbase ca-2025-12-and-2026-01, ca-2026-06 (F-CA2606-030)

items.title: International Sports 2026 — World Cup & Multi-sport Games
items.body:
**In one line.** The 2026 football World Cup, Commonwealth Games, Asian Games and Winter Olympics — hosts, winners and India's showing.

**Why it is asked.** Hosts, next-edition hosts and India's medal rank are repeat questions across these four events.

**FIFA World Cup 2026** (football).
- Co-hosted by **USA, Canada and Mexico**; the first with **48 teams** and 104 matches (11 June-19 July 2026).
- **Spain beat Argentina** in the MetLife Stadium (New Jersey) final for its **2nd title** (first since 2010); the first World Cup final with a halftime show. The next edition (2030) is Spain-Portugal-Morocco.

**Commonwealth Games 2026 — Glasgow.**
- A slimmed 10-sport edition (23 July-2 August); **India finished 4th with 39 medals** (ahead of Scotland on golds); boxing was India's best sport (10 medals, 7 gold).
- **Ahmedabad hosts CWG 2030** (the centenary edition); India becomes the 2nd nation after Australia to host twice (after Delhi 2010).

**Asian Games 2026 — Aichi-Nagoya, Japan.**
- The **20th Asian Games**, 19 September-4 October 2026, motto **'Imagine One Asia'**. Nagoya is Japan's 3rd host after Tokyo (1958) and Hiroshima (1994); it marked 75 years since the first Games (New Delhi, 1951). Next: **Doha 2030**.

**Winter Olympics 2026 — Milano-Cortina, Italy.**
- Hosted across northern Italy (Milan and Cortina d'Ampezzo). France hosts the 2030 Winter Olympics.

**Don't confuse.** The CWG *2030* centenary is in Ahmedabad; India's *2026* CWG result was 4th place — do not merge the host and the result.
keyPoints: 2026 FIFA World Cup: first 48-team edition, co-hosted by USA/Canada/Mexico; Spain beat Argentina for its 2nd title.
CWG 2026 (Glasgow): India finished 4th with 39 medals; Ahmedabad will host the centenary CWG 2030.
2026 Asian Games (20th) were held at Aichi-Nagoya, Japan (19 Sep-4 Oct), motto 'Imagine One Asia'; next is Doha 2030.
2026 Winter Olympics were hosted by Italy (Milano-Cortina).
India first hosted the Asian Games (1951) and the CWG contingent debuted in 1934.

items.title: Nobel Prizes 2025
items.body:
**In one line.** The six 2025 Nobel laureates and the rules behind the prizes.

**Why it is asked.** Nobel laureates and their fields are tested each year, and the exam often misattributes a laureate to the wrong category or city.

**The six 2025 laureates**

| Category | Laureate(s) | For |
|---|---|---|
| Physics | John Clarke, Michel Devoret, John Martinis | Macroscopic quantum tunnelling in electric circuits |
| Chemistry | Susumu Kitagawa, Richard Robson, Omar Yaghi | Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) |
| Medicine | Mary Brunkow, Fred Ramsdell, Shimon Sakaguchi | Peripheral immune tolerance / regulatory T cells |
| Economics | Joel Mokyr, Philippe Aghion, Peter Howitt | Innovation-driven economic growth |
| Literature | László Krasznahorkai (Hungary) | Body of literary work |
| Peace | María Corina Machado (Venezuela) | Democratic rights in Venezuela |

**Exam frame.**
- The **Peace Prize** is decided in **Oslo** by the **Norwegian Nobel Committee**; the other five are decided in **Sweden** (Stockholm).
- Economics is officially the **Sveriges Riksbank Prize** (since 1969), not one of Alfred Nobel's original prizes.
- **Nobel 2026** laureates are announced in October 2026; where this bank already carries them, use the 2026 names, otherwise rely on the 2025 list.

**Don't confuse.** Only the **Peace Prize** is awarded in **Oslo (Norway)**; all the others are decided in **Sweden** — a classic swap.
keyPoints: Nobel Physics 2025: Clarke, Devoret, Martinis (macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits).
Nobel Chemistry 2025: Kitagawa, Robson, Yaghi (metal-organic frameworks/MOFs).
Nobel Medicine 2025: Brunkow, Ramsdell, Sakaguchi (peripheral immune tolerance, regulatory T cells).
Nobel Peace 2025: María Corina Machado (Venezuela); Literature 2025: László Krasznahorkai (Hungary).
The Peace Prize is awarded in Oslo (Norwegian Nobel Committee); the other prizes are decided in Sweden.

items.title: India's Diplomacy & Trade 2025-26
items.body:
**In one line.** India's trade deals, bilateral partnerships and multilateral moves in 2025-26.

**Why it is asked.** FTA dates, named partnership projects (Sabang Port, Project UNICORN) and India's UNSC bid are precise facts examiners like to test.

**Trade agreements.**
- The **India-UK CETA** (Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement) came into force on **15 July 2026**: the UK gives zero-duty access to nearly **99% of Indian exports**. Its **Double Contribution Convention** extends the UK National Insurance exemption for Indian workers posted temporarily to the UK from 12 to 60 months, benefiting 75,000+ professionals.
- India joined the **WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies** as the **123rd member** — the **WTO** (World Trade Organization)'s first environment-focused pact (aquaculture and inland fisheries are excluded).

**Bilateral partnerships.**

| Partner | Outcome (2025-26) |
|---|---|
| New Zealand | Strategic Partnership and 'Roadmap to 2030' (first Indian PM visit in about four decades) |
| Indonesia | Joint development of **Sabang Port** (near the Strait of Malacca) |
| Japan | **Project UNICORN** — the first India-Japan defence co-development (16th summit) |
| Russia | **'Programme 2030 for Strategic Economic Cooperation'** (23rd summit; trade about USD 68-69 billion) |
| Seychelles | ₹1,250-crore Line of Credit and a UPI launch (50 years of ties) |

**Multilateral.**
- India will contest a **UNSC** (United Nations Security Council) non-permanent seat for 2028-29 (Tajikistan is also contesting the Asia-Pacific seat). The UNSC (1945) has 15 members — 5 permanent members with a veto and 10 elected for two-year terms.
- India's **Chief Election Commissioner chairs International IDEA for 2026** (a Stockholm-based democracy body set up in 1995).

**Don't confuse.** The India-UK CETA entered force on **15 July 2026** — not when it was merely signed or announced earlier.
keyPoints: India-UK CETA came into force on 15 July 2026, giving zero-duty UK access to ~99% of Indian exports.
India became the 123rd member of the WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies, the WTO's first sustainability pact.
Key 2025-26 partnerships: NZ Strategic Partnership/Roadmap 2030, Indonesia's Sabang Port, Japan's Project UNICORN, Russia's Programme 2030.
India will contest a UNSC non-permanent seat for 2028-29; the UNSC has 15 members (5 permanent with veto, 10 elected for 2 years).
India's Chief Election Commissioner chairs International IDEA (Stockholm) for 2026.

items.title: Global Indices, Organisations & Geopolitics 2025-26
items.body:
**In one line.** India's global index ranks, the heads of key international organisations, and the main geopolitical flashpoints of 2025-26.

**Why it is asked.** Ranks, organisation heads and founding years are classic matching questions; the exam swaps a head or a headquarters city.

**India in global indices**

| Index | India's rank | Publisher |
|---|---|---|
| Global Innovation Index (GII) 2025 | 38th (from 81st in 2015) | WIPO |
| Global Terrorism Index 2026 | 13th (Pakistan worst) | IEP, Sydney |
| UN SDG Index 2026 | 94th (score 68.3) | SDSN |
| Global Peace Index 2026 | Iceland No.1 | IEP |
| World Bank income class (FY27) | Lower-Middle-Income | World Bank |

**International organisations (founding / HQ / head in 2026).**
- **WTO** (World Trade Organization; 1995, Geneva) — Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala; **IMF** (International Monetary Fund; 1944, Bretton Woods; Washington) — Kristalina Georgieva; **World Bank** — Ajay Banga; **UN Secretary-General** — António Guterres; **WHO** (World Health Organization; 1948, Geneva) — Tedros Adhanom.
- **IAEA** (International Atomic Energy Agency; 1957, Vienna; Nobel 2005); **WFP** (World Food Programme; 1961, Rome; Nobel 2020).

**Geopolitics and AI diplomacy.**
- 2025-26 flashpoints: a **Gaza ceasefire** framework, the **Russia-Ukraine war**, and the **2026 Iran war** (which forced cancellation of the football Finalissima). US trade tools: **Section 301** (Trade Act of 1974) and Section 232.
- The **IndiaAI Impact Summit (February 2026)** was the first such summit hosted by a Global South country, with a 92-nation declaration; China launched the **World AI Cooperation Organization (WAICO)** at Shanghai.
- **Sarnath** was inscribed as India's **45th UNESCO World Heritage Site**.

**Don't confuse.** The **IMF** head is Georgieva and the **World Bank** head is Ajay Banga — options frequently swap these two Washington-based chiefs.
keyPoints: India: GII 2025 = 38th, Global Terrorism Index 2026 = 13th, UN SDG Index 2026 = 94th; still Lower-Middle-Income (World Bank).
Org heads 2026: WTO — Okonjo-Iweala, IMF — Georgieva, World Bank — Ajay Banga, UN SG — Guterres, WHO — Tedros.
IAEA (Vienna, 1957) and WFP (Rome, 1961) are Nobel Peace laureates (2005 and 2020).
US Section 301 (Trade Act of 1974) underpins its tariff actions; 2025-26 saw Gaza, Ukraine and the Iran war.
IndiaAI Impact Summit (Feb 2026) was the first by a Global South nation; China set up WAICO in Shanghai; Sarnath became India's 45th UNESCO site.

items.title: International Timeline — November 2025 to January 2026
items.body:
A month-wise ledger of the biggest international events in the run-up window, with why each matters.

**November 2025**

| Date | What happened | Why it matters for the exam |
|---|---|---|
| 25 Oct (signed) | **UN Convention Against Cybercrime** opened for signature in **Hanoi**; 72 states signed — the first legally binding global cybercrime treaty | Treaty name and host city |
| 12 Nov | **Australia-Indonesia Treaty on Common Security** concluded (builds on the 2006 Lombok Treaty); Iceland flags **AMOC collapse** (a weakening Atlantic ocean current) as a national-security threat | Treaty pairing and a science term |
| 18 Nov | US designates **Saudi Arabia** a **Major Non-NATO Ally** (first Arab state slated for F-35s) | Diplomacy recall |
| 20 Nov | **7th Colombo Security Conclave**, New Delhi — **Seychelles** admitted as a full member | New member recall |
| 22-23 Nov | **G20 Johannesburg Summit** — first on African soil; theme 'Solidarity, Equality and Sustainability'; **ACITI** (Australia-Canada-India) partnership launched | Host-continent fact |
| Nov | India re-elected to the Codex Executive Committee (Asia); India-US 2.2 MTPA LPG deal for 2026; UNSC Resolution 2805 on peacebuilding; India-Israel FTA first step | Multiple quick facts |

**December 2025**

| Date | What happened | Why it matters for the exam |
|---|---|---|
| Dec | **Mamady Doumbouya** elected President of **Guinea** (military leader since the 2021 coup; 7-year term) | Head-of-state recall |
| Dec | **46th GCC Summit** in **Bahrain**; push for a joint air-defence shield (GCC = Gulf Cooperation Council) | Summit host |
| Dec | **Asia Power Index 2025** (Lowy Institute): India **3rd**; **Global AI Vibrancy Index 2025**: India 3rd (US 1st, China 2nd) | Index ranks |
| Dec | Andrej Babiš (**ANO** party) returns as **Prime Minister of Czechia** after the 2025 election | Head-of-government recall |

**January 2026**

| Date | What happened | Why it matters for the exam |
|---|---|---|
| 27 Jan | **16th India-EU Summit**, New Delhi — **FTA negotiations concluded** (begun 2007); 'Comprehensive Strategic Agenda: Towards 2030'; Bharat 6G Alliance-6G-IA MoU | FTA milestone |
| Jan | **Henley Passport Index 2026**: India **80th**; India announces its first **India-Arab Summit** (New Delhi, Feb 2026) | Index rank and summit |
| 1 Oct 2025 (in force) | **India-EFTA TEPA** — USD 100 billion EFTA investment pledge over 15 years (EFTA = European Free Trade Association; TEPA = Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement) | Trade-deal recall |

**Remember it:** G20 Johannesburg (Nov 2025) = first on African soil; India-EU FTA talks concluded 27 Jan 2026.
keyPoints: Oct-Nov 2025: 72 nations signed the UN Convention Against Cybercrime in Hanoi — the first binding global cybercrime treaty.
22-23 Nov 2025: G20 Johannesburg was the first on African soil (theme 'Solidarity, Equality & Sustainability'); ACITI (Australia-Canada-India) partnership launched.
Nov 2025: US made Saudi Arabia a Major Non-NATO Ally; Seychelles joined the Colombo Security Conclave; UNSC Resolution 2805 reviewed peacebuilding.
Dec 2025: Mamady Doumbouya elected President of Guinea; 46th GCC Summit in Bahrain; India 3rd in the Asia Power Index 2025.
27 Jan 2026: 16th India-EU Summit concluded FTA talks (begun 2007) and adopted the 'Comprehensive Strategic Agenda: Towards 2030'.

items.title: International Timeline — February to September 2026
items.body:
Scheduled and announced international milestones for February to September 2026, plus the year's key observances, with why each matters.

**Summits and scheduled events**

| When | What happened | Why it matters for the exam |
|---|---|---|
| Feb 2026 | **IndiaAI Impact Summit** (New Delhi, first by a Global South nation); **India-Arab Summit** (New Delhi); **World Governments Summit** (Dubai); **Winter Olympics** open at Milano-Cortina, Italy | Four flagships clustered in one month |
| 2026 | **G7 presidency: France** (52nd summit); 2025 was Kananaskis, Canada (51st) | Host-country rotation (G7 = Group of Seven industrial democracies) |
| 15 Jul 2026 | **India-UK CETA** enters into force (zero-duty on about 99% of Indian exports) | Trade-deal date |
| 23 Jul-2 Aug | **Commonwealth Games**, Glasgow — India 4th (39 medals) | India's medal rank |
| 8 Sep 2026 | **Khalilur Rahman (Bangladesh)** becomes President of the **81st UN General Assembly session** (from Annalena Baerbock, Germany) | UNGA presidency recall |
| 19 Sep-4 Oct | **Asian Games**, Aichi-Nagoya, Japan (20th edition) | Host and edition |
| 9-20 Nov 2026 | **COP31**, Antalya, Turkey (Australia presides over negotiations) | Climate-summit host |

**Key international days by month**

| Date | Day |
|---|---|
| 2 Feb / 21 Feb | World Wetlands Day (Ramsar 1971) / International Mother Language Day (UNESCO) |
| 3 Mar / 8 Mar | World Wildlife Day (CITES 1973) / International Women's Day |
| 7 Apr / 22 Apr | World Health Day (WHO founded 1948) / Earth Day (since 1970) |
| 3 May / 22 May | World Press Freedom Day / International Day of Biological Diversity |
| 5 Jun / 21 Jun | World Environment Day / International Day of Yoga |
| 11 Jul | World Population Day (UNFPA) |
| 12 Aug / 19 Aug | International Youth Day / World Humanitarian Day (2003 Baghdad bombing) |
| 8 Sep / 16 Sep / 21 Sep | International Literacy Day / World Ozone Day (Montreal Protocol 1987) / International Day of Peace |

**Ongoing environment negotiation.** The **Global Plastics Treaty**: the INC process (the Intergovernmental Negotiating Committee, set up by a 2022 UNEA mandate under the UN Environment Programme, UNEP) is working towards a legally binding treaty on plastic pollution.

**Remember it:** France holds the 2026 G7 presidency; the India-UK CETA entered force on 15 July 2026.
keyPoints: Feb 2026 clusters four flagships: IndiaAI Impact Summit, India-Arab Summit, World Governments Summit (Dubai) and the Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics.
France holds the 2026 G7 presidency (52nd summit); the 2025 summit was at Kananaskis, Canada.
8 Sep 2026: Khalilur Rahman (Bangladesh) becomes President of the 81st UNGA session, succeeding Annalena Baerbock (Germany).
Key days: World Health Day 7 Apr (WHO, 1948), Yoga Day 21 Jun, World Ozone Day 16 Sep (Montreal Protocol, 1987), Peace Day 21 Sep.
The Global Plastics Treaty is being negotiated via the INC under UNEP's 2022 UNEA mandate.

items.title: Exam-Precision: SCO Tianjin, M23/DRC & the 18th BRICS Summit
items.body:
**In one line.** Three precision facts: the 2025 SCO host city, the 18th BRICS host, and where the M23 rebels operate.

**Why it is asked.** These exact host cities and the conflict location are the pin-point details that decide a one-mark question.

**Summits.**
- The **SCO** (Shanghai Cooperation Organisation) **Heads-of-State Summit 2025** was hosted by **China at Tianjin**.
- The **18th BRICS Summit (2026)** is hosted by **India in New Delhi**; India has held the BRICS chair since **1 January 2026**.

**Conflict.**
- The **M23 rebels** are active in **Eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC)**, part of the Great Lakes region conflict, with repeated seizures of territory in North Kivu.

**Don't confuse.** The 2025 SCO summit was at **Tianjin (China)**, while the 2026 BRICS summit is in **New Delhi (India)** — keep the two host cities apart.
keyPoints: The SCO Heads-of-State Summit 2025 was hosted by China at Tianjin.
The 18th BRICS Summit (2026) is hosted by India in New Delhi.
The M23 rebels operate in Eastern DRC as part of the Great Lakes conflict.
items.source: Vajiram summits 2025-26; Indian Express UPSC-Essentials IR (verified Sep 2026)
